text:
Assistant A answers all three parts of the question: it defines the dogma, lists the processes (replication, transcription, translation), and says Crick named it, giving the date 1958. It has one weak point: the explanation of the name is inaccurate. Crick reportedly used "dogma" mistakenly, thinking it meant an idea without supporting evidence, rather than as an analogy to infallible religious teaching. Even so, A's answer is far more complete.

Assistant B gives a minimal definition and then adds basic facts about DNA, RNA, and proteins. It never lists the processes (replication, transcription, translation), so it misses the second part of the question. It does correctly say Crick named it.

A is better because it addresses every part of the question, despite the flaw in its explanation of the name.

[[A]]
